**My thinking as this farmer:**

I have been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years, same as my father before me. The soil here on the North China Plain is deep and flat — good for nothing but wheat and corn, and that is fine with me. The grain station buys both, and I know exactly what to do with them.

My children have all gone to the city. I manage the land alone mostly, about 6 mu in total. I hire the village machinery cooperative for the big jobs — ploughing, harvesting — my back cannot take that anymore at my age. But I still do the fertilizing and irrigating myself.

For wheat, I will plant in October after the summer corn comes off. I will use the improved Jimai variety seed that the seed shop sells — everyone around here uses it and it has done well for me. I plough before planting, put down base fertilizer, then topdress at jointing stage. Four waterings are needed: before sowing, before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. Skip one and the yield suffers badly — I learned that the hard way years ago. Two pesticide sprays: one for aphids in spring, one for rust if I see it.

For summer corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. No time to plough deep — I do rotary tillage to turn the stubble under and plant the same week. Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as my neighbors. I water twice unless August rains are good. Corn mostly takes care of itself compared to wheat.

I do not change what works.
